editorial:
Imagine a world where a silly bet leads to a complete mess of a romance. You get a Los Angeles lawyer who thinks he is too smart for his own good. He decides to answer an ad from a beautiful woman in Chicago who is actually just writing a story for a magazine. The vibe is light and breezy, like those classic romantic comedies where everyone is lying to each other, but you just want them to figure it out already. It is a fun game of cat and mouse where both lead characters are trying to outsmart the other while pretending to be someone they are not.

The acting is snappy and the chemistry between the leads makes the whole thing work. While the plot is a bit predictable, the jokes land well and the pacing keeps you moving. It might feel a bit dated since it is from the eighties, but that just adds to the charm. If you are looking for something easy to watch on a lazy Sunday, you should definitely check this out. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection for a cozy movie night at home.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the lies finally catch up to both characters. The lawyer realizes he actually loves the woman, and she admits she has fallen for him too, despite her reporting assignment. They both confess the bets and the secret motives behind their relationship. Instead of staying mad, they decide to ditch the games and the bets to start a real relationship based on honesty. They end up together in a happy, romantic finale.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school romantic comedies and funny misunderstandings.
